title: Partial feature-profile compatibility review
software_contract: review_profiles(request) validates all rules and all profiles before assessing any profile. Invalid input raises ValueError; message text is unspecified. Do not mutate the request. For each profile return whether its fixed feature settings can be extended to a full Boolean configuration satisfying all catalogue rules. requires=[a,b] means if a is enabled then b is enabled; excludes=[a,b] means they cannot both be enabled; each at_least_one group requires one or more listed features enabled. Repeated rules/features inside rule groups are allowed. A self-requirement is always satisfied; a self-exclusion forces that feature disabled. An empty at_least_one group makes every configuration invalid. Return feature_count, profile_count, profiles, compatible_profile_ids and incompatible_profile_ids. Profile reports preserve profile input order and contain profile_id, enabled, disabled, unfixed_features, completion_exists (bool). The three feature lists follow declared feature order, not alphabetical or profile input order. The ID summary lists preserve profile order. Empty profiles produce empty report/ID lists after full rule validation. Zero features can have a valid empty configuration if rules do not contain an empty group. Return exact existence decisions, not a witness, probability or unverified absence claim. CLI reads one JSON request and prints one report; invalid input produces no successful report and a nonzero exit.
input_domain: JSON object with exactly features, requires, excludes, at_least_one, profiles. features is a finite list of unique nonempty strings. requires/excludes are lists of two-element lists of known feature names, including self-pairs. at_least_one is a list of lists of known names, including empty lists. profiles is a list of objects with exactly profile_id (unique nonempty string), enabled and disabled (lists of distinct known names, mutually disjoint). All feature names are case-sensitive. There is no numerical maximum feature count in the source contract; bounded regression inputs do not change the domain.
execution_assumptions: A profile fixes only its listed features; all others remain available for completion. There is no objective to minimize enabled features or choose a preferred completion.
Ordinary classical JSON is supplied. No hardware, resource budget, latency target or measured benefit is provided.
